judge_assessment.explanation: The judge's mathematics is right and its one error is real but understated. I recomputed all eight orders from worksheet.tex: plates of 5/8/3 -> 3,5,8; cards 7/4/9 -> 4,7,9; ten-frames of 6/10/3 -> 3,6,10; cube trains of 13/7/11 -> 7,11,13; shelves -> 12,20,21; jars 41/14/40 -> 14,40,41; Ben = 8+3 = 11 so 6,8,11; Red 15 / Blue 20 / Gold 12 so 12,15,20. All agree with the key. On the delivery error: pdfinfo gives worksheet.pdf 3 pages against the response's '2 pages' -- confirmed -- but the same response also calls the study guide '1 page' when study_guide.pdf is 2, so two of the three page counts it states are wrong, not one. The judge also did not look at the Quick Answers bank, where the multi-entry problems render as '7. 11, 6, 8, 11' and '8. 15, 12, 12, 15, 20' -- the hidden totals concatenated with the answer, so the bank reads like a four- and five-number answer when the student writes three. ACCEPT is still right.

strengths_to_preserve: Problems 7 and 8 do the thing the rest of this shard fails to do: each hidden total is a SEPARATE eval entry alongside the ordering compare entry (id 7 = eval 8+3 -> 11 plus compare [8,11,6] -> [6,8,11]; id 8 = eval 10+5 -> 15, eval 9+3 -> 12, compare -> [12,15,20]). A right order built on a wrong total cannot pass. That is the multi-entry-per-id pattern the verify-every-printed-answer-slot fix should generalise, and it already works.

Problem 6 uses 41 / 14 / 40 on purpose -- the digit-reversal error -- and the study guide's watch-out box closes the loop on it ('14 and 41 use the same two digits but they are not the same amount'). The key's reasoning compares tens first, then ones, rather than just asserting the order.

Every problem ends with the identical 'least ___ ___ ___ greatest' answer strip, so a five-year-old always knows what a finished answer looks like, while the representation underneath changes eight times (plates, cards, ten-frames, cube trains, shelf counts, jar counts, a 'more than' story, two-part team totals).

root_causes.description: final_response.md states page counts from the author's expectation rather than from the compiled PDFs. The build already knows the real counts -- scripts/page_budget.py reads them out of the engine log for the compile gates -- but nothing feeds them into the delivery text.
evidence: final_response.md: 'Study guide (ss_ordering_curr013.pdf, 1 page)'; pdfinfo study_guide.pdf -> Pages: 2

root_causes.description: render_entry() in scripts/render_quick_answers.py comma-joins every entry under an id with no role marker, so intermediate values that the student never writes on the answer strip appear inside the banked answer.
evidence: the answers the student actually writes are '6, 8, 11' and '12, 15, 20'

improvements.title: Page counts in the delivery text must come from the compiled PDFs
improvements.proposed_change: scripts/build.sh already parses the page count of each PDF for the compile-ws / compile-ak / compile-ss budget gates. Print those three numbers in the final gate summary block, and add a SKILL.md delivery rule that the response must quote the printed numbers rather than an estimate (or simply omit page counts).
improvements.regression_test: In tests/test_page_budget.py, assert the gate summary emitted by a successful build contains a line of the form 'pages: ws=N ak=N ss=N'. The summary has no such line today.
improvements.expected_impact: Removes the whole class of 'delivery describes the worksheet as two pages, the PDF has three' findings -- the only defect the judge recorded for this case, and a repeat offender across the run.
improvements.risk: Very low; additive output, no gate semantics change.

improvements.title: Multi-entry problems concatenate intermediate results with the final answer in the bank
improvements.proposed_change: render_entry() in scripts/render_quick_answers.py comma-joins every entry's 'expected' for an id, with no marker of which value is the answer the student writes. Separate the roles: either honour an optional "role": "step" / "final" tag on each entry and bank only the final one (with the steps in parentheses), or at minimum join with an arrow ('11 -> 6, 8, 11') so a grader can see where the intermediate work stops and the answer begins.
improvements.regression_test: In tests/test_render_quick_answers.py, render an id carrying an eval entry (expected 11) followed by a compare entry (expected [6, 8, 11]) and assert the bank line is not the flat string '11, 6, 8, 11'. Fails today; passes once the roles are distinguished.
improvements.expected_impact: Removes bank lines that read as a four- or five-number answer when the student writes three (curr-013 entries 7 and 8) or one (curr-038 entry 8).
improvements.risk: Low; presentation-only, and no gate reads the bank text.

case_summary: A strong representations-and-applications sheet on ordering three quantities. All eight orders and the three hidden totals recompute correctly, the ramp from picture (plates, ten-frames, cube trains) to bare numerals to two-step stories is genuine, and 41/14/40 is a well-chosen trap that the study guide explicitly teaches against. Its verification is the best in my shard: problems 7 and 8 carry an entry per computed quantity, so eleven checks cover eight problems. Two defects, both in the delivery layer rather than the mathematics: the response misstates two of the three page counts (worksheet 2 vs the actual 3, study guide 1 vs the actual 2), and the Quick Answers bank concatenates intermediate totals into entries 7 and 8.
